story.head: The Islanders’ edge in depth
paras: The Jets won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-3 in overtime in Winnipeg on Nov 19. The Jets come in at 11-9-3, the Islanders at 10-6-5. Going in, the Jets are sixth in the Central (tied for 15th in the NHL) and the Islanders fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 15th).
The Jets’ record (.543) is about what their chances are worth. The Islanders’ record (.595) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.492), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Jets create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (3rd), get their shots through to the net (4th) and rarely ice the puck (5th). The Islanders get their defensemen shooting (1st) and have had the league’s best goaltending (1st). They also roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), so the Isles have the edge over the Jets on depth.

Mark Scheifele (7 G / 22 A / 29 P in 23 GP) leads the Jets in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against the Islanders. Kyle Connor (18 G / 10 A / 28 P in 23 GP) has a team-high 18 goals, tied for third in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. For the Islanders, Matthew Schaefer (9 G / 15 A / 24 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Bo Horvat (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 21 GP) isn’t far behind.

Stuart Skinner (7-5-3 / .883 SV% in 16 GS) is in line to start for Winnipeg. Ilya Sorokin (8-4-2 / .918 SV% in 14 GS) has been a rock in net for the Islanders and will likely start. Sorokin has a .876 save percentage in five starts against the Jets, well under his usual .909. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
